children.translated_text: Composed by the <s>yoginī Lakṣmīṅkarā</s>
<s>Advayasiddhi</s> (Accomplishment of Non-Duality)
Oṃ. Homage to the glorious <s>Vajrasattva</s>.
Having bowed my head to the Lord who is luminous by nature (<s>prakṛtiprabhāsvara</s>), omniscient, arisen from the three realms of existence,
the <s>vajra</s> (diamond/thunderbolt) that grants the fruit of all desired aims,
without [regard for] place, time, lunar day, weekday, constellation, or <s>maṇḍalas</s>,

children.text: vakṣye haṃ vajrasattvasya saṃkṣepāt sādhanaṃ param //
children.translated_text: I shall briefly expound the supreme <s>sādhana</s> (practice) of <s>Vajrasattva</s>.
Through disciplines, vows, fasting, utterance of syllables, and [mere] meditation,
[this is] non-reality yoga (<s>atattvayoga</s>);
[one who practices thus is] a non-reality yogin (<s>atattvayogī</s>)—
[such a one] will not attain <s>siddhi</s> (accomplishment) even in hundreds of <s>koṭis</s> (ten millions) of <s>kalpas</s> (cosmic ages).
With <s>viḍvajra</s> (impure substances), water, seeds, and the like, arising from within the nostrils,
the <s>mantra</s>-practitioner should constantly worship the self through <s>tattva</s>-meditations (<s>tattvabhāvana</s>).
One's mother, sisters, daughters, and nieces—
the knower of <s>yoga</s> should always worship [them] through the method of <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom) and <s>upāya</s> (skillful means).
A one-limbed woman, a deformed woman, a craftswoman, an outcaste woman (<s>śvapacī</s>)—
one should always worship [such] women through the radiance of <s>jñānavajra</s> (knowledge-thunderbolt).

Here are the seed-syllables: o

children.text: yena yena hi baddhyante jantavo raudrakarmaṇā /
children.translated_text: By whatever [means] beings are bound through fierce actions,
by that very [means], through skillful method (<s>upāya</s>), they are freed from the bondage of existence (<s>bhavabandha</s>).
One should perform the divine <s>samayas</s> (observances) day after day, arising from the five families (<s>pañcakula</s>);
and one should worship with lamps and other [offerings], with milk, arising from the universe.
The <s>mantra</s>-practitioner, with wide-open eyes, always with a smiling face,
placing the mind upon awakening (<s>saṃbodhi</s>), should meditate on the ocean of knowledge (<s>jñānasāgara</s>).

children.text: yāvat sthiracalā bhāvā santy atra tribhavālaye /
children.translated_text: As long as there are states both stable and moving in this triple abode of existence (<s>tribhavālaya</s>),

children.text: sarve te tattvayogena draṣṭavyā vajradhṛg yathā //
children.translated_text: all of them should be seen through <s>tattvayoga</s> (reality-yoga) as [identical with] the <s>vajra</s>-holder (<s>Vajradhṛk</s>).
And certain followers of other doctrines (<s>paravādin</s>), established through distinctions of religious marks (<s>liṅga</s>),
even they should not be despised here, [for they are] transformations of <s>Vajrasattva</s>.
Having made all states of being equal in one flavor (<s>samarasīkṛtya</s>), arisen from selflessness (<s>nairātmya</s>),
the <s>mantra</s>-practitioner should constantly meditate on the body as pure by nature (<s>prakṛtinirmala</s>).
With fragrances, garlands, and other [offerings], with cloths, incense, and food-offerings,

children.text: gītavādyais tathā nṛtyaiḥ sopāyair bhajate vibhuḥ //
children.translated_text: with songs, music, and dances, the all-pervading Lord (<s>Vibhu</s>) worships through skillful means (<s>upāya</s>).

children.text: na kaṣṭakalpanāṃ kuryān nopavāsaṃ na ca kriyām /
children.translated_text: One should not make painful ascetic constructions, nor fasting, nor [ritual] actions;
neither bathing nor purification here, nor avoidance of worldly conduct.
Nor should one worship gods made of wood, stone, or clay;

children.text: pūjām asyaiva kāyasya kurvān nityaṃ smāhitaḥ //
children.translated_text: one should constantly perform worship of this very body, with concentrated mind.
With [offerings] mixed with fly-vomit, with feces, urine, and other [substances] that have been meditated upon,
combined with five lamps, one should worship the <s>vajra</s>-holder (<s>Vajradhārin</s>).
With a woman's self-born flowers (<s>svayambhukusuma</s>, menstrual blood), with milk, arising from the universe,
one should worship the deity dwelling in the body through <s>tattva</s>-meditations.
One should steal others' property; one should engage with others' wives;

children.text: vaktavyaṃ ca mṛṣāvākyaṃ sarvabuddhāṃś ca ghātayet //
children.translated_text: one should speak false words; and one should slay all <s>Buddhas</s>.
One should not make <s>caityas</s> (shrines) of stone or clay; nor delight in books;
nor [create] <s>maṇḍalas</s> even in a dream, through actions of body, speech, and mind.
The knower of <s>mantras</s> should not feel disgust toward any substance;

children.text: vajrasattvaḥ svayaṃ tatra sākṣād rūpeṇa saṃsthitaḥ //
children.translated_text: <s>Vajrasattva</s> himself is directly present there in [his own] form.
The distinction of what is proper and improper to approach, what is proper and improper to eat,

children.text: peyāpeyaṃ tathā mantrī kuryān naiva samāhitaḥ //
children.translated_text: what is proper and improper to drink—the concentrated <s>mantra</s>-practitioner should never [make such distinctions].
Living beings (<s>prāṇaka</s>) arisen from <s>Vairocana</s>, born from the limbs of all sentient beings—
the knower of the secret <s>tattva</s> should consume [them] as a cause of <s>siddhi</s> (accomplishment).
Women born from all <s>varṇas</s> (social classes) should not be despised;

children.text: saiva bhagavatī prajñā saṃvṛtyā rūpam āśrityā //
children.translated_text: she herself is the Blessed <s>Prajñā</s> (Wisdom), having assumed form through conventional reality (<s>saṃvṛti</s>).

children.text: na tithir na ca nakṣatraṃ nopavāso vidhīyate /
children.translated_text: No lunar day, no constellation, no fasting is prescribed;
for one endowed with non-dual knowledge (<s>advayajñāna</s>), Buddhist <s>siddhi</s> (accomplishment) arises.

children.text: bahunātra kim uktena yad bhaved upalabdhikam /
children.translated_text: What need is there to say more here? Whatever is apprehensible (<s>upalabdhika</s>),
all that should be seen through <s>tattvayoga</s> (reality-yoga) by the knower of <s>tattva</s>.
Lamps [made from the fat] of elephants, horses, donkeys, cattle, camels, and dogs—
the knower of <s>yoga</s> should always consume [these], mixed with the great lamp [substance].

children.text: na cādhyāsaktiṃ kurvīta ekasminn api yogavit /
children.translated_text: The knower of <s>yoga</s> should not make excessive attachment to even a single [thing];
the ocean of existence (<s>bhavārṇava</s>) should be meditated upon through the <s>yoga</s> of equanimous mind (<s>samatācittayoga</s>).
Arising, abiding, and cessation—unassociated with ordinary beings (<s>pṛthagjana</s>);

children.text: tasya bhāve tu saṃsāro nānyatra pralayodbhavaḥ //
children.translated_text: in the state of that [realization], <s>saṃsāra</s> [itself becomes nirvāṇa]; dissolution and origination are nowhere else.

children.text: dinaṃ tu bhagavān vajrī naktaṃ prajñā vidhīyate /
children.translated_text: The day is [presided over by] the Blessed <s>Vajrī</s> (the vajra-holder); the night is designated as <s>Prajñā</s> (Wisdom);

children.text: evaṃ tu bhāvayed yogī laghu siddhim avāpnuyāt //
children.translated_text: thus the <s>yogin</s> should meditate; [then] one swiftly attains <s>siddhi</s>.

children.text: yat tad avyaktarūpaṃ tu sarvasattveṣu saṃsthitam /
children.translated_text: That which has an unmanifest form, established in all sentient beings—

children.text: guruvaktrāt paraṃ tattvaṃ prāpyate nātra samśayaḥ //
children.translated_text: that supreme <s>tattva</s> (reality) is obtained from the mouth of the <s>guru</s>; there is no doubt about this.
The <s>nirvāṇa</s> that is foundationless (<s>apratiṣṭhita</s>), uncaused, without abode —
pervading all sentient beings, perfect awakening (<s>saṃbodhi</s>) is the supreme state.

children.text: evaṃ matvā tu vai yogī yo 'bhyased buddhimān sadā /
children.translated_text: The wise <s>yogin</s> who, having understood this, always practices —

children.text: sa siddhyati na sandeho mandapuṇyo 'pi mānavaḥ //
children.translated_text: he attains perfection (<s>siddhi</s>), without doubt, even a man of little merit.
There is nothing higher than the teacher (<s>ācārya</s>) in the three worlds of moving and unmoving [beings] —
by whose grace, perfections (<s>siddhi</s>) of many kinds are obtained by the wise.

children.text: vajrasattvaḥ sa vai jñeyaḥ sarvabuddhair namaskṛtaḥ /
children.translated_text: He is to be known as <s>Vajrasattva</s>, bowed to by all <s>Buddha</s>s —
the teacher is the supreme deity, to be worshipped with [utmost] effort.
He himself, having the form of suchness (<s>tathatā</s>), for the sake of benefiting beings,
having assumed form conventionally (<s>saṃvṛti</s>), is stationed at the <s>yogapīṭha</s> (yoga-seat).

children.text: mṛtyur eṣa vikalpo yaṃ na bhāvaḥ sarvavastuṣu /
children.translated_text: This conceptual construction (<s>vikalpa</s>) is death — there is no [inherent] existence in any things.
One is slain by one's own conceptual construction, [amidst] the proliferations of ordinary beings.

children.text: śrīmadoḍīyānavinirgatā mahāyogapīṭhāgatā 'khilayogatantratattvagarbhā śrīlakṣmīmukhakamalād viniḥsṛtā svādhiṣṭhānakramodayā advayasiddhir nāma sādhanopāyikā samāpteti
children.translated_text: Issued from the glorious <s>Oḍḍiyāna</s>, arrived at the great <s>yogapīṭha</s>, containing the essence of all <s>yoga-tantra</s> principles, emanated from the lotus-mouth of the glorious <s>Lakṣmī</s> [<s>Lakṣmīṅkarā</s>], arising in the sequence of self-empowerment (<s>svādhiṣṭhānakrama</s>) — the <s>Advayasiddhi</s> (Accomplishment of Non-Duality), a manual of practice (<s>sādhanopāyikā</s>), is thus completed.
